newsitem.title: JAPAN: Polls close in Okinawa referendum over U.S. bases.
newsitem.headline: Polls close in Okinawa referendum over U.S. bases.

text.p: Polls closed at 6 p.m. (0900 GMT) in Sunday's vote by residents of Okinawa on whether the huge U.S. military presence on the Japanese island should be reduced, with signs that the turnout was lukewarm.

All involved predicted a "yes" vote, with the key issue the size of the turnout. Officials said that 30 minutes before the polls closed, 54 percent of the eligible voters had taken part, far less than the 70 percent supporters had wanted as a clear mandate.
The relatively low turnout gives a freer hand to Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto in deciding when to call a general election.

Political observers had said that a more decisive vote would have forced the prime minister to come up with new measures to reduce the U.S. military presence, which takes up 20 percent of the land on Okinawa's main island. The province, 1,500 km (930 miles) from Tokyo, has 50 inhabited islands in all.
At issue is the size of the bases, as well as the specifics of the Status of Forces Agreement which governs the legal status of U.S. military personnel in Japan.
Officials said they expected to have specific figures on the vote by 10 p.m. (1300 GMT).
